scope: Selected primary publications relevant to Parkinson forecasting; targeted comparison, not a systematic review.
comparison_rule: No numerical difference or model ranking without matched geography, year, age, sex, estimand, units and evaluation design. Published values retain their reported precision. Historical GBD releases are recorded as provenance, not labelled contradictions.

su_2025_bmj.citation: Su D, Cui Y, He C et al. Projections for prevalence of Parkinson's disease and its driving factors in 195 countries and territories to 2050: modelling study of Global Burden of Disease Study 2021. BMJ 2025;388:e080952.
su_2025_bmj.model: Bayesian model averaging of six models
su_2025_bmj.verification: Primary full text and Table 1 checked. Country supplementary PDF returned a browser challenge; exact Saudi 2024-2028 values were not verified. This does not establish that such values do not exist.

wu_2025_frontiers.citation: Wu XC, Dong YY, Ying YC et al. The burden of Parkinson's disease, 1990-2021: a systematic analysis of the Global Burden of Disease study 2021. Front Aging Neurosci 2025;17:1596392.
wu_2025_frontiers.verification: Primary full text, section 3.6 and Figure 6 description checked. Global forecasts are age-standardised rates, not Saudi age-specific rates or counts.

marras_2018_npj.citation: Marras C, Beck JC, Bower JH et al. Prevalence of Parkinson's disease across North America. NPJ Parkinsons Dis 2018;4:21.
marras_2018_npj.model: Stable age-sex prevalence estimates applied to projected population
marras_2018_npj.data_source: North American observational prevalence studies; US Census population projections
marras_2018_npj.verification: Primary abstract and Results checked. US age-45+ projections, reported approximately to thousands; not a Saudi forecast.

published_forecasts.source_locator: Results: Projected prevalence of Parkinson's disease from 2022 to 2050
published_forecasts.comments: Global 2030 estimate; contextual comparison only. Both studies combine disease-rate and population forecasts. No Saudi difference or accuracy ranking is valid; published millions converted to people without adding precision.

Table 1 supplies more precision than the abstract. Global 2050 burden is not numerically comparable to Saudi 2028 burden; thousands converted to people. Uncertainty bounds do not establish empirical coverage.

published_forecasts.source_locator: Table 1: North Africa and Middle East; 2050 number of cases (thousands)
published_forecasts.comments: Regional context including Saudi Arabia, not a Saudi forecast. Different geography, age range and forecast year prevent direct differences. Published thousands converted to people.

Same five-year forecast horizon, but global ASR cannot be compared numerically with Saudi 45+ counts or individual age-specific rates. The paper uses ARIMA; our study evaluates transfer learning against statistical comparators. Bounds were not numerically extracted.

Published incidence forecast supplies five-year ARIMA context. Global ASR and Saudi annual incident counts are different estimands; no percentage difference or accuracy ranking is calculated. Bounds were not numerically extracted.

published_forecasts.source_locator: Abstract and Results: US 2030 age-45+ projected cases
published_forecasts.comments: Same 45+ restriction and count estimand. US geography and 2030 endpoint differ. Stable age-sex prevalence is applied to census projections, whereas our disease rates are forecast. Reported approximate precision retained; no forecast bounds extracted.
